Tension Error and Load Cell PID$N$Np29r10_tension_error is the explicit tension error in lbf.  It replaces$Np29r10_pid_psn.ERR everywhere it was consumed (p01r13_winder_tension_ok$Nand the p29r17 diameter calculation), so no logic outside this routine$Ndepends on PID block internals any more.$N$NThe PID itself is OUT OF THE CONTROL PATH.  Winder speed trim now comes$Nfrom the proportional accumulator position block below.  The PID is held$Nin manual permanently with SO tracked at 50 so that it cannot wind up and$Nthe HMI faceplate shows a sane output.  Block and tags are kept declared$Nfor HMI back-compat - delete the PID instruction if the faceplate goes.$N$NRev 20260820

Tension Loop Selection - which loop holds web tension$N$NACCUMULATOR ON   air pressure holds tension.  The carriage position trim$N                 drives winder speed, and this PID is parked in manual$N                 with its output tracking that trim so the handover is$N                 bumpless.$N$NACCUMULATOR OFF  pressure is zero and the carriage sits on its stop, so$N                 nothing pneumatic holds tension.  This PID goes to auto$N                 on the winder load cell and trims winder speed - the$N                 original pre-accumulator control.$N$NWithout this the accumulator work left NOTHING controlling tension when$Nthe accumulator is switched off: speed_offset came only from carriage$Nposition, and with the carriage resting at 0 percent against a 10 percent$Npark setpoint the trim clamped at its minimum and held the winder at$N0.8 x line speed indefinitely.  pid_psn_cv had no consumer at all.$N$NSO is preloaded as offset x gain + 50, the inverse of the offset$Ncalculation, so auto picks up exactly where the trim left off.$N$NRev 20260904 a38

If param_psn_gain is too big, fabric will not take up.$NIf it is too small, you get oscillation.$NBig number means small PID error addition to winder speed.$NNormal running, need 100.$NTurret rotation need 80.$NAt start of 3$Q roll, need 40 for about 5 seconds$NUse the 3$Q/6$Q SS for operator control of faster/slower.$NThe 3$Q-6$Q core switch is used to provide manual pickup speed.

Divisor guard - psn_gain$N$Npsn_gain divides the PID output twice, and param_psn_gain is adjustable$Nfrom the HMI.  Zero faults the processor outright; a very small value is$Njust as bad without the fault - at 0.1 the speed offset reaches +/-500,$Nwhich is a runaway rather than a trim.$N$NFloored at 10, which still allows eight times the normal 80 in$Naggressiveness and caps the offset at +/-5.$N$NPlaced after both selection rungs so it covers the running gain and the$Nindex gain alike.$N$NRev 20260904 a40

Accumulator Position to Winder Speed Trim$N$NStrict proportional, no integral.  Explicit setpoint and explicit gain:$N$N   error = carriage position - p29_param_acc_park_sp$N   trim  = error x p29_param_acc_trim_gain$N   trim  clamped to [p29_param_speed_trim_min, p29_param_speed_trim_max]$N$NDefaults - park 10%, gain 0.02 per % of stroke, clamp +/-0.20:$N$N        0%  ->  -0.20   winder 0.80 x line, accumulator refills$N       10%  ->   0.00   park, winder at line speed, in balance$N       20%  ->  +0.20   winder 1.20 x line, drawing down$N   above 20%  ->  +0.20  clamped - this IS the payout overspeed$N$NNothing commands the carriage to the park position.  Park is simply where$Nthe trim crosses zero, and the loop settles there by negative feedback:$Nabove park the winder outruns the line and the carriage falls, and the$Ntrim shrinks as it approaches.  Steady state offset from park is$N(persistent surface speed error) / gain - a 1% speed mismatch parks it$N0.5% of stroke off, and it clamps only at a 20% mismatch.$N$NThis replaces a SYS_SCP block that mapped 0-20% onto -0.20/+0.20.  That$Nworked, but the park position was implicit - it was the midpoint only$Nbecause the two trim limits were symmetric, so changing the negative$Nauthority silently moved where the accumulator lived (trim_min -0.10 with$Ntrim_max +0.20 would have parked it at 6.7%).  Setpoint, gain and$Nauthority are now three independent parameters.$N$NWhy proportional only:  carriage position is the INTEGRAL of the speed$Ndifference.  P on an integrating plant is a first order closed loop - it$Ncannot oscillate on its own and needs no integral term to remove offset.$NIt also holds no state, so there is no windup and no manual/auto handover.$N$NIf it ever hunts at high line speed, widen the band by REDUCING$Np29_param_acc_trim_gain - do not reduce the trim clamp, that is the payout$Nauthority and is now a separate number.$N$NThe load cell PID does not drive speed.  See the rungs above.$N$NRev 20260820 a02

At 1 PLI the$Ntare masked it (34.6 vs 35.3 psi); at 2.5 PLI it was 40.3 psi against a$Nrequired 58.1 - the accumulator would have held about a third of the$Ntension asked for, and worse the higher the setpoint.$N$NThe 83 lbf offset is the carriage: 83 x 16.59/4 = 344 lb, consistent with$Nthe mechanical note that the carriage must fall under its own weight.$N$NRev 20260829 a32

Filling and Emptying Pressures$N$NTwo curves, not one pressure plus a bias.  Filling needs more pressure$Nthan emptying for the same web tension, and the gap is not constant -$N3.7 psi at 1 PLI, 6.0 psi at 2.5 PLI.  A fixed param_fill_bias_psi could$Nnot represent that, so it is gone.$N$N  wac_tension_pressure  = (tension + 83) / 4.14 + trim    emptying, hold$N  filling_pressure      = (tension + 83) / 3.75 + trim    fill request$N$Nparam_tare_pressure is now a TRIM, starting at 0.  The vendor curve$Nalready carries the carriage weight in the 83 lbf offset, and is stated$Nto exclude friction between parts.  Any standing offset found at install$N- seal drag, guide friction - goes here.  It is no longer the whole$Nintercept, so do NOT set it to 30.8.$N$NCheck against the vendor table at install:$N$N  PLI   tension lb   fill psi   empty psi$N  1.0        63        38.9       35.3$N  1.5        94.5      47.3       42.9$N  2.0       126        55.7       50.5$N  2.5       157.5      64.1       58.1$N$NRev 20260829 a32

Accumulator Pressure Select$N$NDESIGN INTENT:  the accumulator is transparent to web tension.  The web$Nsees the same tension with the accumulator in the loop as it would with$Nthe accumulator bypassed, in every state where the web is flowing through$Nto the winder.$N$NThe cylinders are a constant-force device.  Pressure sets web tension; it$Ndoes NOT set carriage position.  Carriage position is set by the mass$Nbalance between what the line feeds in and what the winder draws out.$N$NRungs are in order of increasing priority - the last rung to write$Nselected_pressure wins:$N$N  1  Normal run                 wac_tension_pressure$N  2  Payout                     wac_tension_pressure$N  3  Fill request               filling_pressure  (steeper fill curve)$N  4  Fault, or line not moving  wac_tension_pressure$N$N1, 2 and 4 are all the same pressure, and that is the point - nothing$Nabout accumulator state changes web tension.  During payout the carriage$Ndescends because the winder is overspeeding and drawing web out faster$Nthan the line feeds it in, not because pressure was reduced.$N$NThe position PID offset is NO LONGER added to the running pressure.  Any$Nposition trim on the pressure is a tension disturbance by definition, so$Nthe carriage is left to float.  PID_offset now reaches the web only$Nthrough the fill bias in rung 3, where the exit nip is closed and the$Nwinder is isolated from the accumulator.$N$NSuperseded, no longer used:  payout_pressure (fixed 29 psi),$Nparam_holding_pressure (fixed 14 psi), tension_pressure (fixed 35 psi).$N$NRev 20260820

Payout Status and Carriage Position Publish$N$NThe winder speed trim is now a strict proportional function of carriage$Nposition, done with a scaling block in p29r10 / p29r11:$N$N        0%  ->  -0.20      winder at 0.80 x line, accumulator refills$N       10%  ->   0.00      park, in balance$N       20%  ->  +0.20      winder at 1.20 x line, drawing down$N   above 20% ->  +0.20      saturated - this IS the payout overspeed$N$NBecause that curve is continuous there is no payout-to-running handover$Nto sequence and no cross-fade. They$Nno longer gate any speed logic.  Latch is at park + 2% so that a short$Ndoff which only part-fills still shows payout; unlatch at park, with$Nwac_nearly_empty kept as a backstop.$N$NRev 20260820

Payout Activation$N$NPayout only runs into a winder that can actually take the web:$N$N  winder A active AND turret at winder A run position, OR$N  winder B active AND turret at winder B run position$N$Nvia p29_winder_at_run_position.
